articles.originalTitle: Contemporary Istanbul founder planning new fair on city's Asian side - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Contemporary Istanbul Founder Planning New Fair on City's Asian Side
articles.excerpt: As Türkiye's largest contemporary art fair Contemporary Istanbul hosts around 70 galleries for its third year at Tersane Istanbul, founder Ali Güreli announced plans to launch a new fair on the Asian side.
articles.content: The 21st edition of Türkiye's largest contemporary art fair took place at Tersane Istanbul on the Golden Horn with around 70 participants. Occupying a 6,000 sq. m. single-floor site, the event hosted galleries from over 15 countries. Fair founder and chairman Ali Güreli announced that the event will return in 2027 while detailing future plans to launch another fair on the city's Asian side. Güreli also added that his venture is in talks with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism regarding an art taxation reform similar to Italy's recent tax cuts. The event featured international galleries such as Jessica Silverman Gallery, Galeria Karla Osorio, and Pearl Lam Projects, alongside local participants. Meanwhile, the fair's official solution partner, Numeraire Future Trends, conducted demonstrations on biometric authentication and value assessment for physical artworks throughout the event.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Unveils New Timepieces at Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe showcased limited-edition timepieces inspired by the Italian market and new collections at the seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe hosted the seventh and largest edition of its Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan. Staged at CityOval Milano across 31,215 square feet, the exhibition traces the brand's history and contemporary innovations with over 500 items, including the 1868 wristwatch owned by Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Patek Philippe president Thierry Stern noted that Italy represents a long-standing market of connoisseurs. During the event, the manufacturer debuted seven limited-edition timepieces featuring casebacks inscribed with the Milan 2026 detail, including three Calatrava models representing the Italian flag and world-time repeaters depicting downtown Milan. The exhibition also marked the introduction of the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry watch collection. Running through October 18, the event coincides with Milano Watch Week.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - Architectural Record
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Relocates to Historic Warehouse Building
articles.excerpt: The MIT architecture department has moved into its new home inside a 195,000-square-foot converted historic warehouse designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro and Leers Weinzapfel.
articles.content: Having occupied scattered spaces across the campus for over a century, the MIT architecture department relocated to a 195,000-square-foot converted warehouse in Cambridge. The 500-foot-long brick structure, with its oldest portion dating to 1894, was redesigned by Diller Scofidio + Renfro alongside Leers Weinzapfel. Originally built as the Metropolitan Storage Warehouse, the property was acquired by MIT in 1962. The conversion project frames the reconstitution of existing structures as a creative act of design. Named the Met Warehouse, the building houses the architecture and urban studies and planning departments, alongside the Morningside Academy for Design, an initiative promoting cross-disciplinary design. To fit these programmes into a masonry structure with low ceilings, the architects employed a strategy of cutting and subtraction. Multistory voids were carved within the blocks, and lightweight structures suspended from the roof created column-free studios and gathering spaces. The design team also integrated supportive interventions such as concrete shear walls and steel framing to maintain the historic structure.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: New East County Library Opens in Gresham, Oregon, Featuring Mass-Timber Structure
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture, the 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, has been completed at a cost of $163 million to serve the local community.
articles.content: The new East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, addresses the wider region's long-unmet needs while setting a precedent for future development. Designed by Holst Architecture, the two-story building features mass timber columns and fluted ultra-high-performance concrete panels that evoke regional forests. Located 17 miles east of Portland, the facility was developed in response to population growth and demographic shifts in East Multnomah County. Spanning 95,000 square feet, the library project cost $163 million. The design process involved extensive community outreach, resulting in programmatic additions such as a reservable auditorium, rooms for neurodivergent users, and a recording studio. The building utilizes a Type IV heavy-timber system featuring 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed without additional fire-resistant treatments. The design team integrated mechanical conduits within the timber structure through specialized detailing. Fortis Construction served as the general contractor for the facility, which reached completion in May 2026.

articles.originalTitle: design museum gent reopens with new wing built from locally made waste bricks - Designboom
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Reopens Following Four-Year Renovation and Expansion Project
articles.excerpt: Design Museum Gent in Belgium reopens on October 3, 2026, following a multi-year renovation featuring a new wing constructed from locally produced waste bricks.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent in Belgium reopens on October 3, 2026, following a four-year renovation and expansion led by Carmody Groarke and ATAMA, with historic buildings restored by RE-ST. The project introduces a 2,200-square-meter wing designed to function as an open civic space with areas for exhibitions, workshops, lectures, and community activities. The extension features timber and a facade made from over 82,000 Gent Waste Bricks, which are lime-cured products derived from locally sourced municipal waste including minced concrete, glass, car windscreens, and porcelain. The reopening program features multiple exhibitions, including Collection, which places around 500 objects from the 24,000-piece archive into contemporary themes such as copy, comfort, migration, folds, and connections. Another opening presentation, Public Matter(s): Design and Democracy, examines democratic systems as designed structures through historical contexts and interactive formats like the Democracy Fitness Trail. The architectural intervention integrates fragmented historic buildings around a central courtyard that now functions as a garden and orientation point. Organized across six operational zones ranging from basement art handling to the top-floor Loft, the renewed museum balances the preservation of historic interiors with contemporary structural additions.

articles.originalTitle: Step inside the revamped Ghent Design Museum, a ‘touchpoint' for coming together - wallpaper.com
articles.title: Ghent Design Museum Reopens Following Extensive Expansion and Heritage Restoration
articles.excerpt: Belgium’s largest design museum has reopened following a major expansion and restoration led by Carmody Groarke and Atama, featuring a new low-carbon wing built with local municipal construction waste.
articles.content: Belgium’s largest design museum, Ghent Design Museum, has reopened following an extensive expansion, consolidation, and heritage restoration project led by British architects Carmody Groarke alongside local architects Atama. The project introduced a new circulatory loop through historic buildings and a low-carbon entrance wing. The new wing was built using lime-cured bricks developed from Ghent’s municipal construction rubbish with a grant from Circular Flanders, holding one-third of the embodied carbon of standard clay-fired Belgian bricks. Standing at five storeys, the timber-structured wing features a 3D-printed recycled aluminium entrance gate designed by Unfold. Excavations at the site also uncovered the remains of a 12th-century residential structure, identified as the oldest-ever found in Ghent. Guided by the vision of museum director Katrien Laporte, the revamped site includes a spacious foyer, a café with a courtyard garden, and experimental workshop spaces. Architect Andy Groarke described the building as a scaffold for young designers to test ideas and collaborate in a physical space.

articles.originalTitle: São Paulo’s Museu de Arte Moderna reopens after two-year renovation - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: São Paulo Museum of Modern Art Reopens After Two-Year Renovation
articles.excerpt: Having closed its doors for two years of renovations, the São Paulo Museum of Modern Art has reopened with an exhibition designed to push the boundaries of Brazilian art.
articles.content: The Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo (MAM) has resumed operations in its Oscar Niemeyer-designed pavilion in Ibirapuera Park following a two-year closure for renovations. Reopening on 12 September, the institution chose to debut not with its permanent collection, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art, titled Depois Que Tudo Foi Dito (After It's All Said), running until 24 January 2027. Chief curator Cauê Alves noted the symbolic return to the exact pavilion that hosted the inaugural Panorama in 1969. During the closure, the museum maintained an active profile by organizing over a dozen exhibitions in partner venues. Curated by Diane Lima, the current edition features 33 artists and engages with philosophical perspectives on representation, colonialism and racial violence. Lima explained that the participating artists explore form and materiality rather than fulfilling expected tropes associated with Black, Indigenous and dissident backgrounds. The reopening exhibition serves as a statement on the institution's evolving relationship with its public and artistic boundaries.

articles.originalTitle: Arthur Jafa at the New Museum, Review: A Horror Show for the Ages - artnews.com
articles.title: New Museum Opens Expansive Survey Exhibition Dedicated to Arthur Jafa
articles.excerpt: The New Museum in New York presents "I Am Tony," a major survey exhibition spanning four decades of work by artist Arthur Jafa.
articles.content: The New Museum in New York is presenting "I Am Tony," a major survey exhibition dedicated to the artist Arthur Jafa. On view through January 3, the exhibition spans nearly four decades of Jafa's artistic output across two floors of the museum. Curated by Massimiliano Gioni and Gary Carrion-Murayari, the installation casts much of the gallery space in darkness to highlight Jafa's visual art rather than his cinematic background. The exhibition brings together works ranging from his early binder series Notebooks to the remade automotive sculpture MBD_Trans Am and the computer-generated video AGHDRA. Jafa's perspective that Black existence is intrinsically bound with horror informs much of the presentation, evoking a pervasive sense of danger through recurring motifs of monsters, cinematic appropriations, and unsettling soundscapes. The immersive project underscores the collision of terror and beauty that defines Jafa's oeuvre, offering visitors a nonlinear journey through his influential body of work.

articles.originalTitle: ‘He said the secret to a happy life is attention to the details’: William Morris Gallery reopens after major rehang and restoration - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: William Morris Gallery Reopens Following Major Restoration and Rehang
articles.excerpt: The William Morris Gallery in Walthamstow, London, is reopening this Saturday following a major rehang and revamp marking the 130th anniversary of the artist's death.
articles.content: Located in a manor in Walthamstow, northeast London, where the artist lived as a teenager, the William Morris Gallery is reopening this Saturday after transforming six gallery spaces in its first major overhaul since 2012. Timed to mark the 130th anniversary of Morris's death, the project led by architect Sam Jacob and gallery director Hadrian Garrard introduced a more domestic sensibility to the institution through community consultation and detailed restoration. The rehang addresses Morris's complex biography, contrasting his privileged background with his socialist ideals, including an information desk crafted from copper in memory of workers from his father's mine. Funded with approximately 1.5 million pounds raised from trusts such as the Garfield Weston Foundation and the Wolfson Foundation alongside the Waltham Forest Council, the gallery reopens alongside an exhibition titled Earthly Paradise: Radical Living in the UK.

articles.originalTitle: Open call: Commissions for English Ceramic Circle Centenary display at V&A South Kensington - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A and English Ceramic Circle Launch Open Call for Centenary Display
articles.excerpt: The English Ceramic Circle has announced plans to commission up to new works for a centenary display at V&A South Kensington, with submissions closing on November 15, 2026.
articles.content: The English Ceramic Circle, the largest and oldest society dedicated to the study of British ceramics and enamels, is marking its 100th anniversary with a special display at V&A South Kensington. Running from October 2027 to September 2028, the exhibition will highlight artistic and technological contributions from potters working in Britain from 1600 to the present. To support this display, the circle is seeking to commission up to three new works through an open submission process aimed at UK-based ceramic artists. Organizers particularly encourage proposals from early- and mid-career practitioners with between 3 and 15 years of experience working with clay. Selected artists will receive a fee of 3,000 pounds per artist and will work alongside curatorial staff to develop their projects. Finished works must be delivered to the museum by September 2027 for exhibition in Room 146. Applications require a 300-word artist statement and a 500-word proposal detailing the idea, physical form, dimensions, and materials. The deadline for submissions is November 15, 2026, with successful applicants notified in December 2026. The acquired works will ultimately be donated to a public museum in the UK following the conclusion of the display.

articles.originalTitle: The Luxembourg Pavilion Examines Overconsumption of Living Space Through "Excess!" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale - ArchDaily
articles.title: Luxembourg Pavilion to Examine Living Space Consumption at 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
articles.excerpt: The Luxembourg Pavilion at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale will address the overconsumption and inequitable distribution of living space through a curatorial proposal titled 'Excess!'
articles.content: A jury of arts and architecture professionals announced the selected curatorial proposal for the Luxembourg Pavilion at the Biennale Architettura 2027. Titled 'Excess! On the Overconsumption of Living Space,' the exhibition is curated by housing expert Céline Zimmer alongside architects Bùi Quý Sơn and Paul-Antoine Lucas, co-founders of Exutoire. The proposal addresses the inequitable distribution of living space as a reflection of broader habits contributing to current housing and ecological crises. The issue will be illustrated through a dialogue between the realities of Luxembourg and Vietnam to reflect on spatial consumption. Located on the first floor of the Sale d'Armi in the Arsenale, the Luxembourg Pavilion will open to the public on May 8, 2027. The curatorial team draws on professional experience in housing systems, social justice through design, and queer theory in architecture to open up conversations and learn from intersecting perspectives. The upcoming Venice Architecture Biennale will run from May 8 to November 21, 2027, featuring the overarching theme 'Do Architecture — For the Possibility of Coexistence Facing a Real Reality,' curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu.

articles.originalTitle: Christine Sun Kim, Rodney McMillian, Vincent Valdez Win MacArthur ‘Genius’ Grants - artnews.com
articles.title: MacArthur Foundation Announces 2026 Fellowship Recipients Including Four Artists
articles.excerpt: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation has announced the 20 recipients of its annual fellowship grants, including four artists.
articles.content: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation has announced the 20 recipients of its annual MacArthur Fellowships, commonly known as Genius Grants, which provide 800000 dollars in unrestricted funds to each fellow. This year's cohort includes four artists: Christine Sun Kim, Rodney McMillian, Vincent Valdez, and Chip Thomas. Christine Sun Kim creates works that challenge institutional ableism related to Deafness, while Rodney McMillian's multidisciplinary practice examines how socioeconomic conditions and history influence quality of life. Vincent Valdez focuses on racism and the Latinx experience through historical and contemporary paintings, and Chip Thomas produces community-grounded public art primarily within Navajo Nation. Poet Layli Long Soldier is also among the 2026 fellows, having influenced generations of Native artists with her poetry. Kristen Mack, the foundation's vice president for communications, noted that the new fellows continue a 45-year tradition of defying boundaries, questioning conventions, and expanding the edges of inquiry and research.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces exhibitors and showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach Edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Announces Exhibitors and Layout for 2026 Miami Beach Edition
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries and territories at the Miami Beach Convention Center, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and focused gallery line-up for its 2026 edition.
articles.content: Art Basel has announced the exhibitor line-up for the 2026 edition of Art Basel Miami Beach, which will feature 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center, the fair runs from December 4 to 6, with VIP Preview Days scheduled for December 2 and 3. Drawing on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee, the 2026 fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout. The new plan occupies approximately 12% less floor space, while the main sector, Galleries, features approximately 10% fewer exhibitors. The space is organized around four hospitality plazas instead of five to create longer sightlines and improve navigation. More than 30 galleries are participating for the first time, largely through project-based sectors such as Nova, Positions, and Survey. Latin America and the Caribbean are represented in depth, with Brazil forming the third-largest national contingent. Los Angeles and Chicago contribute notable participation, alongside a strengthened South Florida presence. Zero 10, the global initiative for digital-era art, returns with a presentation including projects by artists such as Jon Rafman, Refik Anadol, and Sarah Meyohas. Global Lead Partner UBS supports the event.

articles.originalTitle: Digital Art Committee - Centre Pompidou
articles.title: Centre Pompidou Establishes Five-Year Digital Art Committee
articles.excerpt: The Centre Pompidou has announced the establishment of a Digital Art Committee for a five-year period to support digital art, fund acquisitions, and contribute to research programmes.
articles.content: The Centre Pompidou has established a Digital Art Committee bringing together French and international patrons to support the institution's commitment to digital art and raise its profile in this area. Operating for five years, the programme will fund the acquisition of works for the Centre Pompidou - Musée National d'Art Moderne collection, support promotion and sharing policies for digital art, and back conservation operations on artworks. The initiative continues the institution's history with computer-assisted creation, following the 1975 establishment of the Studio of Research in Advanced Techniques. In 2023, the institution became the first modern and contemporary art museum to acquire a set of works related to the blockchain. In recent years, the new media collection has also acquired its first works using virtual reality and augmented reality. Furthermore, a partnership with KADIST has fostered reflections around artificial intelligence, leading to several acquisitions in this area. During this period, the museum carried out research into the earliest decades of computer-assisted creation, adding works from the 1960s to the 1990s to its collection.

articles.originalTitle: David Bowie’s unrealised projects - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Archive Explores David Bowie's Unrealised Film and Musical Projects
articles.excerpt: The David Bowie Archive houses handwritten notes, scripts, and storyboards detailing the late performer's unrealised film and musical projects developed throughout his career.
articles.content: Material preserved within the David Bowie Archive offers insight into multiple creative projects that the performer worked on throughout his career without ever fully realising them during his lifetime. The collection features film scripts, storyboards, lyrics, and research notes that document Bowie's artistic process. Between 1973 and 1974, Bowie collaborated on a musical-comedy adaptation of George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four with director Tony Ingrassia, writing a treatment and multiple songs that later influenced the Diamond Dogs album and tour. Other archival holdings detail the Young Americans film project, which followed an astronaut on a mission to the moon in a dystopic 1950s America, differing significantly from the 1975 album of the same name. Additional unrealized works documented in the archive include The Catastrophy Cabinet television film, a planned biographical collaboration titled All The Emperor's Horses alongside David Kidd, and Neutron, an apocalyptic science fiction film developed in partnership with Derek Jarman and Lee Drysdale during the 1980s.

articles.originalTitle: Talk Art: Brilliant: Unexpected Art from Everywhere (Livestream) - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum to Host Talk Art Podcast Event
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host a live recording of the Talk Art podcast to celebrate the publication of the book Brilliant: Unexpected Art from Everywhere. The online event tickets cost 8.00 pounds.
articles.content: Hosted by actor Russell Tovey and gallerist Robert Diament, the Talk Art podcast is holding a special live recording event to celebrate the publication of the book Brilliant: Unexpected Art from Everywhere. Hosted by the Victoria and Albert Museum, the event will feature interviews with contemporary photographers whose work appears in the book, including Keerthana Kunnath, Tami Aftab, and Mous Lamrabat. Curated by WePresent and published by Monacelli, the book brings together visual works that have never been published in print before. Addressing themes such as cultural memory, immigration, the female gaze, and the internet, the collection spans diverse subjects from explorations in Senegal and Qatar to the production processes of award-winning short films. The online event will take place on Zoom on 2 November 2026. Tickets are priced at 8.00 pounds, and general booking opened on 5 October. Ticket holders will receive a link to view the morning event live, and a recording will remain available for viewing for one month following the talk.

articles.originalTitle: A way of looking: our first encounter with the Cochin Ceiling - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Researchers Visit Victoria and Albert Museum to Study Cochin Ceiling
articles.excerpt: Ananth Ramaswamy and Devi Seetharam examined the historic Cochin ceiling in person as part of the Victoria and Albert Museum South Asia Gallery commission. The researchers explored the museum collection to contribute to the gallery refurbishment scheduled to open in 2028.
articles.content: Ananth Ramaswamy and Devi Seetharam examined the historic Cochin ceiling in person for the first time as part of the Victoria and Albert Museum South Asia Gallery commission. The 19th-century carved polychromed teak coffered ceiling panels from Kerala were observed during museum conservation work. The researchers had the opportunity to directly compare wood samples and finishes against the historic artifact alongside the conservation team. During the visit, the polychromy and intricate carvings of the ceiling were closely observed, and hundreds of objects were examined across the museum galleries and archives. Tracing the motifs of the lotus through art and architecture, the researchers studied various ceramic and metal objects from the museum collection. The contemporary commission will form part of the transformed South Asia Gallery, scheduled to open in 2028. The refurbishment project is supported by The National Lottery Heritage Fund, Dunard Fund, Mandakini Puri, and additional donors.

articles.originalTitle: 12 uplifting design stories we discovered in Finland this month - wallpaper.com
articles.title: Helsinki Design Week Showcases Urban Innovation and Creative Growth in Finland
articles.excerpt: Helsinki Design Week highlighted innovative urban design projects, circular architecture, and collaborative creative strategies across the Finnish capital this September.
articles.content: Held in September, Helsinki Design Week brought together innovative design approaches aimed at enhancing urban habitats and everyday life. A strategic planning document commissioned by the City of Helsinki's Economic Development Division outlined nine key actions for growing the creative sectors alongside urban development. During the event, architect Pekka Airaxin launched Kainuu, a new company delivering turnkey summer houses constructed from cross-laminated timber sourced from managed forests within an 80 km radius. Kainuu has already delivered 10 houses, with 20 more in the pipeline. Additionally, Finnish architect and theorist Juhanni Pallasmaa donated his entire 10,000-strong book collection to Helsinki's Architecture & Design Museum in honor of his 90th birthday, with 10 percent of the collection currently on display at a temporary space. Hotel refurbishments and material-led experimental projects further highlighted the city's ongoing design engagement.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Step-Free Access Upgrades Completed at Surrey Quays and Northolt Stations in London
articles.excerpt: Transport for London has completed step-free access upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations, improving accessibility for wheelchair users, parents, and older travelers across the rail and tube networks.
articles.content: Transport for London has completed step-free access improvements at Surrey Quays and Northolt railway stations, enabling journeys for wheelchair users, pushchair users, and travelers with luggage. At Surrey Quays on the London Overground, a new entrance, ticket hall, footbridge, accessible toilets, baby changing facilities, and two new lifts were delivered. Funded via a housing infrastructure program and a contribution from developer British Land, the project was executed by lead designer AtkinsRealis and contractor Morgan Sindall Infrastructure between January 2023 and September 2026. The construction prioritized low-carbon materials, including CEM 3 concrete and electric arc furnace steel, alongside a green roof and solar panels. Meanwhile, Northolt station on the Central line received a new footbridge and lift to provide step-free access between the street and trains, marking the 95th station on the Tube network to feature step-free access. The Northolt project cost an estimated 15.3 million pounds, running from February 2025 to September 2026. Engineers also regraded and replanted the embankment at Northolt to support biodiversity net gain.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe Exhibition Opens at University of Michigan Museum of Art
articles.excerpt: Black Wall Street Journey, Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027.
articles.content: Rick Lowe's public art project Black Wall Street Journey has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art as the artist's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States. On view in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation to examine how Black prosperity, resilience, and self-determination are represented, measured, and understood. The presentation reflects the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the institution and mirrors his deep engagement with researchers, data scientists, and numerous students. Working collaboratively across art, data, and inquiry, Lowe examines the forces that shape Black wealth and opportunity, ranging from income and education to housing and business ownership.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Works from the Brown Collection on View in London
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition brings together artworks spanning six centuries at the Brown Collection in London.
articles.content: Curated by Glenn Brown and his husband Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must is on view at the Brown Collection through August 7, 2027. The presentation features paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics by more than twenty artists spanning six centuries, incorporating spliced collages, double images, and elongated figures. The exhibition aims to challenge the mechanisms of the mind and create connections between works not typically seen together. Additionally, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly has been published, coinciding with a catalogue raisonné and exhibition dedicated to Brice Marden. In other developments, Adriana Varejão opened her studio to share her working practice as she prepares new works to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, the Brazilian Pavilion features Varejão alongside Rosana Paulino, reflecting on colonial narratives and history.

articles.originalTitle: Why Toronto is fast becoming unmissable for art - artbasel.com
articles.title: Toronto Arts Scene Expands Amid Diversity and Infrastructure Growth
articles.excerpt: Toronto is gaining prominence in the art world through its immigrant population and hybrid cultural fabric. Biennials, new art trails, and independent spaces strengthen the city's infrastructure, while commercial and studio space needs shape ongoing developments.
articles.content: Kenneth Montague, founder of The Wedge Collection, notes that Toronto's hybrid identity and multicultural fabric form the foundation of Canadian art. With 51 percent of its population born abroad, the city hosts a dynamic scene featuring artists showcased at international platforms like the Venice Biennale. Running its fourth edition this current month, the Toronto Biennial centers on the shared geographies of the Great Lakes and Indigenous artists to foster global dialogue. Along the waterfront, the Lassonde Art Trail—backed by 25 million dollars in seed funding from Pierre Lassonde—features 17 new commissions winding through Biidaasige Park. While curators and directors highlight the civic impact of these urban revitalization projects, artists point out that commercial infrastructure remains critical for the ecosystem. Artist-run spaces and newly established downtown studio initiatives maintain a grassroots momentum, while institutions like the Art Gallery of Ontario and MOCA expand their programming and gallery footprints. Local participants observe that while Toronto's collector base holds significant potential, the demand for affordable studio spaces and institutional growth continues as the local arts community navigates rapid urban development.

articles.originalTitle: La vida secreta de las plantas: Anselm Kiefer en la Colección Grothe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Anselm Kiefer Brings The Secret Life of Plants Exhibition to Barcelona
articles.excerpt: Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera–Casa Milà in Barcelona is hosting the first Anselm Kiefer exhibition in the city, bringing together around forty works from the collection of Hans Grothe.
articles.content: Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera–Casa Milà in Barcelona is hosting an exhibition titled The Secret Life of Plants. Scheduled from October 2, 2026, to January 24, 2027, the presentation gathers approximately forty works by Anselm Kiefer from the collection of Hans Grothe, alongside pieces from other private collections. The selection offers insight into the symbolic richness and material complexity of the artist's practice. At the core of the presentation is Opus Magnum, a series of vitrines on display for the first time in Spain. Conceived as archives of memory, these works assemble books, plants, stones, and fabrics in a dialogue between history, myth, science, and spirituality. In parallel, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly has been released, featuring various contributions and previews of upcoming projects. Meanwhile, Adriana Varejão prepared new works destined to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, the Brazilian Pavilion places Varejão in conversation with Rosana Paulino to reflect on colonial wounds and the rewriting of history in Brazil.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collections and Designs Presented at Paris Design Week 2026
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week featured contemporary furniture, lighting, and decor collections rooted in traditional techniques and natural forms.
articles.content: Paris Design Week marked its 16th edition across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond with 500 exhibitors. Draga and Aurel showcased Crisalide side tables featuring fused colored glass and brass bases, while Pinto teamed up with Nobilis to present the warm-toned Foundation collection. Yves Salomon Éditions introduced Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior range inspired by natural forms. Swedish design house Veermakers opened a new showroom in Le Marais, and Nordic Knots presented wool rugs influenced by Swedish Grace. L'Objet partnered with jeweler Jessica McCormack for sea-inspired tabletop objects. Modern Metier exhibited Rudy Guénaire's Tropic of Capricorn collection, and Garnier & Linker unveiled Aurora, an outdoor lighting series. Franck Genser presented his Piscine VI coffee table, and wood-working atelier Hervet Manufacturier displayed its full furniture range during the design week.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Renowned Parisian Hatmaker Maison Michel Celebrates 90th Anniversary With New Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with an exhibition at La Galerie du 19M, highlighting traditional craftsmanship, historic tools, and the intricate journey from raw materials to finished headwear.
articles.content: Renowned Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with a comprehensive exhibition celebrating the intricacies of millinery craftsmanship. Opening on Sept. 23 at La Galerie du 19M, Chanel's craftsmanship hub in northern Paris, the exhibition runs through Dec. 13. Titled "Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel," the display focuses as much on ancient tools and techniques as it does on final designs, offering visitors a detailed look inside the historic workshop. Curated by artistic director Priscilla Royer alongside Palais Galliera fashion museum director Emilie Hammen, the exhibition begins with tree trunks carved into raw hat shapes alongside thousands of wooden hat blocks from the house archives. The showcase highlights traditional methods such as sewn straw using 19th-century machines, alongside specialized works in canvas, organza, leather, and tweed. Throughout the space, specially commissioned artworks, large-scale photographs by Bastiaan Woudt, and a replica of an early 20th-century milliner's shop contextualize the evolution of headwear. Organizers noted that hats have transitioned from restrictive social signifiers into a form of personal expression, while the workshop itself continues to embrace a modern revival in dramatic statement pieces.
